key_claims: Gestational protein restriction programs domain-specific and sexually divergent behavioral and cognitive aging trajectories in offspring.
Low-protein offspring of both sexes were born lighter but caught up in weight by postnatal day 7.
Middle-aged males exposed to gestational protein restriction showed anhedonia-like behavior, anxiety-like behavior, reduced exploration, and impaired short-term object recognition.

Middle-aged females exposed to gestational protein restriction exhibited hyperactivity, stereotypy, and thigmotaxis, and developed anhedonia-like behavior in old age while retaining certain long-term memories.
limitations: The study was conducted in mice, limiting direct generalizability to humans.
Surrogate clock scores do not measure tissue-specific botanical, anti-inflammatory, joint, enzymatic, or mucosal benefits.
what_not_to_say: Gestational protein restriction causes uniform cognitive decline in humans.
Surrogate clock scores measure tissue-specific botanical, anti-inflammatory, joint, enzymatic, or mucosal benefits.
